$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Subscriptions. See aws/s3.json for the contract.

azure.subscriptions.overview.title: Subscription overview (get, rename) over ARM
limitations: Vyomi simulates exactly one subscription — renaming it changes the one simulated subscription's display name rather than creating or listing an independent additional subscription. Offer/Offer ID are a fixed Pay-As-You-Go quotaId (subscriptionPolicies), matching how the real portal looks them up; Parent management group and Secure score are not modeled (no management-group hierarchy or Microsoft Defender scoring exist in Vyomi).

azure.subscriptions.activity_log.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity.

azure.subscriptions.access_control_iam.title: Access control (IAM) — role assignments, roles and checkAccess
limitations: Role assignments are real ARM resources scoped to the subscription they were created under (list + checkAccess only see assignments at that scope, with the same wildcard, scope-inheritance and explicit-deny-wins semantics as the Entra RBAC engine), and the Roles tab + checkAccess cover the built-in Owner/Contributor/Reader/… roles plus any custom role definitions. But checkAccess is a standalone decision tool: no other ARM call in Vyomi consults it, so every other data-plane/control-plane operation still succeeds regardless of what is assigned. Deny assignments and classic administrators are always empty.

azure.subscriptions.resources.title: Resources (Settings > Resources — every resource group in the subscription, at once)

azure.subscriptions.deployments.title: Deployments (Microsoft.Resources/deployments) history, subscription scope
limitations: Deployment creation resolves `[parameters(...)]`/`[variables(...)]` to literal values and actually PUTs every resource listed in properties.template.resources through the same ARM dispatcher, so a deployment really provisions something — but no other ARM template function (concat/resourceId/reference/copy loops) or dependsOn ordering is evaluated, so templates using them fail at the dependent resource's own validation. Cancel always returns a conflict because every deployment completes synchronously before a Cancel call can arrive (the same conflict a real deployment that finished first returns); Redeploy re-runs the same stored template for real.

azure.subscriptions.resource_locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to the subscription itself

azure.subscriptions.usage_quotas.title: Usage + quotas (Microsoft.Compute/Microsoft.Network locations/{location}/usages + Microsoft.Quota)
limitations: Vyomi models a reduced subset of Azure's default regional quotas (Total Regional vCPUs and Virtual Machines for compute; Public IP Addresses, Virtual Networks, Network Security Groups for network). Counts are live off provisioned resources and ENFORCED with the real QuotaExceeded error. Quota increase requests (Microsoft.Quota quotas / quotaRequests) are validated (not below usage, not above 50x the default), auto-approved up to 4x the default and otherwise Failed with the real 'create a support request' message; an approved request really raises the enforced limit. The response lists the counted resource names, which real Azure does not.

azure.subscriptions.security.title: Security (Microsoft Defender for Cloud secure score + recommendations, subscription scope)
limitations: Reuses the same native rule engine as the dedicated Defender for Cloud console (core/azure_security_core.py) — see azure.defender.* in core/capabilities/azure/defender.json for its own limitations (Vyomi's own rule set, not Azure's full built-in catalogue; alerts need runtime workload telemetry Vyomi has none of).

azure.subscriptions.diagnostics.title: Diagnose and solve problems
limitations: The real blade is an interactive catalog of hundreds of service-specific troubleshooting guides (most needing live telemetry Vyomi has none of). Vyomi instead runs concrete, live checks against this subscription's own real state — operations that failed (Activity log), this subscription having no resource lock, and quota usage at or above 80% — and links each finding to the real page that explains and fixes it.

azure.subscriptions.events.title: Events
limitations: Real Azure's Events blade is Service Health (platform outages/planned maintenance) merged with the Activity log. Vyomi has no platform to have outages, so Events shows the same real, subscription-wide Activity log feed Activity log itself uses (core/azure_arm_core.py's Microsoft.Insights/eventtypes), not a separate data source.

azure.subscriptions.advisor_recommendati.title: Advisor recommendations
limitations: Real Azure Advisor evaluates hundreds of rules across Cost/Security/Reliability/Performance/Operational excellence using telemetry (utilization, logs) Vyomi doesn't collect. Vyomi's Advisor instead surfaces genuine findings over real state it DOES have: Security recommendations are the subscription's own Unhealthy Defender assessments (azure.subscriptions.security); Reliability flags critical resources (SQL servers, Cosmos accounts, Key Vaults) with no resource lock; Cost flags resource groups with real spend but no budget configured. No Performance recommendations are produced (no utilization metrics exist to base them on).

azure.subscriptions.invoices.title: Invoices (Microsoft.Billing/invoices)
limitations: Simulated and marked as such: one invoice per month the inventory existed, amountDue is always 0.00 (nothing is billed) and avoidedAmount carries what real Azure would have charged for the resources Vyomi ran (azure_cost_core list prices, accrued from each resource's creation). Deleted resources leave no ledger, so past months are a lower bound; no PDF documents, invoice sections or payment methods.

azure.subscriptions.billing_properties.title: Billing properties (Microsoft.Billing/billingProperties)
limitations: Real ARM makes billingProperties a tenant-scoped singleton; Vyomi keeps it subscription-scoped instead, since it models exactly one subscription anyway. Only the Account admin field is a real, persisted PATCH/GET round-trip. Currency is fixed USD and the rest of the real billing-account hierarchy (billing accounts, invoice sections, agreement type beyond the fixed Pay-As-You-Go offer already on Overview) is not modeled.

azure.subscriptions.preview_features.title: Preview features (Microsoft.Features/providers/{ns}/features)
limitations: Register/unregister persists exactly like real ARM, over a curated sample of real preview feature flag names (not the full live catalog, which changes continuously in real Azure). Toggling a flag doesn't change any OTHER Vyomi behavior — the same ceiling most real preview features have too, since they mostly unlock allow-listing on Microsoft's control plane rather than changing it locally.

azure.subscriptions.my_permissions.title: My permissions (Microsoft.Authorization/permissions)
limitations: Derived live from the same role catalog/assignments checkAccess uses for the one simulated signed-in identity — inherits access_control_iam's limitations (single directory, deny assignments only as far as Vyomi's own RBAC engine models them).

azure.subscriptions.policies.title: Policies (Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions, policyAssignments, Microsoft.PolicyInsights/policyStates)
limitations: Real policy rule engine (core/azure_policy_core.py): built-in definitions by their real GUIDs (Allowed locations, Allowed / Not allowed resource types, Require a tag, Require a tag and its value, Secure transfer to storage accounts) plus CUSTOM policyDefinitions whose policyRule (if/then, allOf/anyOf/not, equals/in/like/exists/contains/…, tags['k'], property aliases, parameters) is evaluated. 'deny' blocks a create/update with RequestDisallowedByPolicy; 'audit' and deny rules feed the Compliance tab, at subscription, resource-group and resource scope.

Not modelled: count expressions, template functions other than parameters()/concat(), auditIfNotExists / deployIfNotExists / modify / append effects (these evaluate as 'NotStarted' and never block), policy initiatives (set definitions), exemptions, remediation tasks and the full Azure built-in catalog (only the six listed). Assignments scoped to a single resource are shown by filtering the resource-group assignments.

azure.subscriptions.deployment_stacks.title: Deployment stacks (Microsoft.Resources/deploymentStacks)
limitations: Inherits the deployments template evaluator's limitations (literal parameter/variable substitution only). What a plain deployment doesn't do: DELETE on a stack really cascade-deletes every resource it manages (actionOnUnmanage.resources: 'delete', the default) unless set to 'detach' — genuine lifecycle enforcement, not just metadata.

azure.subscriptions.programmatic_deploym.title: Programmatic deployment credentials
limitations: This blade's exact real wire call was never captured (reference-only in the spec); Vyomi models its real effect instead — generating a service principal with a real Contributor roleAssignment at the current scope, observable in Access control (IAM) and genuinely enforced by checkAccess (verified by an explicit checkAccess call, not just stored config). The returned client secret cannot actually be redeemed for a token: Vyomi implements no Microsoft Entra OAuth token endpoint for a real SDK/CLI to authenticate against.

azure.subscriptions.management_certifica.title: Management certificates
limitations: Uploaded .cer / PEM certificates are really parsed (DER walk: SHA-1 thumbprint, subject and issuer CN, notBefore / notAfter); expired, not-yet-valid or duplicate certificates are refused and the subscription is capped at 100. They belong to the retired classic deployment model: Vyomi does not authenticate classic Service Management calls with them.

azure.subscriptions.partner_information.title: Partner information (Microsoft.ManagementPartner)
limitations: A Microsoft Partner Network ID (digits only) can be associated, updated and removed; one association per tenant. Vyomi does not look the ID up against the real MPN directory, so the partner name is whatever is entered.

azure.subscriptions.cost_management.title: Cost analysis, budgets and cost alerts, subscription scope

azure.subscriptions.transfer_requests.title: Subscription ownership-transfer requests (Microsoft.Billing/transferRequests)
limitations: Create (validated recipient e-mail, not the current owner, one pending at a time), accept / decline / cancel and a 15-day expiry; accepting really changes the subscription's account administrator. Vyomi has no second tenant, so there is no recipient-side acceptance flow or directory move.

azure.subscriptions.top_free_services.title: Top free services by usage (Microsoft.Billing/freeServices)
limitations: The free-account allowances are a fixed table; usage is MEASURED from the real inventory where possible (hours of free-eligible VM sizes this month, Blob GB, SQL databases, Cosmos accounts) and flagged 'Not measurable' otherwise (Key Vault operations, Functions executions).

azure.subscriptions.marketplace.title: Creating a new resource from the Marketplace (Vyomi Marketplace)
limitations: Vyomi publishes its own SaaS-simulator offers; subscribing creates a real Microsoft.SaaS/resources resource (offer / plan / term validated, one subscription per offer per resource group, plan change, access key rotation, unsubscribe). The third-party vendors' APIs are not emulated and nothing is billed.
